items.note: Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra's three grades of town by size (4,000, 2,000, 1,000 cāpa).
items.gloss: The best town is of four thousand capa (four kos, about twelve km); the middle of two thousand; the lowest is one thousand capa (one kos) in diameter.

items.note: The 64-pada town plan with sixteen compartments, six roads and nine crossings; the royal road on the middle bamboo/axis.
items.gloss: Conceive the whole town as a sixty-four-pada grid, with sixteen kosthas, six paths and nine chatvaras (crossings); divide the square plot into four portions of three vamshas each; in this six-vamsha division of sixteen padas the auspicious royal road should be made on the middle vamsha.

items.note: Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra on town defence: a rampart ground beyond the main roads and three moats, with the excavated earth used for the rampart (vapra).
items.gloss: Set the ground for the rampart outside the ghanta-marga all round; beyond it, in proportion to the great road, dig three moats of wide excavation with intervals; leave a third or half unexcavated; the earth dug from the moat should make the rampart on its own ground, curved, elephant-backed and rammed down by the feet of cows.

items.note: The three moats filled with drain water or flowing water, with lotuses and gardens around.
items.gloss: They should be filled with water from drains or flowing water, delightful with various lotuses, with outlets and crocodiles; around them gardens of flowering trees all round.

items.note: Rampart (prākāra) widths and heights in hastas, graded by city size.
items.gloss: Its width is of three grades: largest twelve cubits, middle ten, smallest eight; the largest rampart is said to be seventeen cubits high, the middle fifteen, the last thirteen; it should be neither above seventeen nor below thirteen cubits.

items.note: Parapet (kapiśīrṣa), turrets (aṭṭālaka) at gates and corners, spaced a hundred cubits apart, making the city impregnable.
items.gloss: A cubit-high kapishirsha (battlement) and a two-cubit kandavarini to stop enemy arrows; build attalakas (watchtowers) joined to the corner supports on the four sides; arranged a hundred cubits apart, the city becomes inaccessible to infantry, horses, chariots and elephants.

items.note: The rampart walkway (carikā) with steps, platform, towers and crenellations.
items.gloss: The carika with the gate-way becomes easy to walk, with platform and steps; build it with turrets (nirvyuha) and battlements (kapishirshaka).

items.note: Gate dimensions and the pratolī (gateway passage) with bolts and bars.
items.gloss: The gate of the main road should be six, five or four cubits high; every main gate should have a strong pratoli with strong bar and indrakila (main peg) with the door's cross-bar; the pratoli should be like the royal road, extending as a hall.

items.note: Third storey over the main gate with defensive apparatus (vyāla, jāla, śataghnī); three-storeyed gate-towers for the city's prosperity, beauty and protection.
items.gloss: Above the main gate make a third floor with a barred-door chamber and circumambulation, set on pillars and platform, equipped with vyala, jala, shataghni and the like; for the city's growth, beauty and protection build large gates with three-storeyed portals all round.

items.note: Covered drains in the city, one or two cubits wide.
items.gloss: In the city, drains covered with stone and wood should be made; these water-drains going round should be of two or one cubit.

items.note: Texts prescribe that a śāstra-knowing sthapati found the city with propitiatory rites (śānti, abhyudayika); work done without rites is inauspicious.
items.gloss: Therefore the sthapati learned in the shastra should settle the city as prescribed; rites of propitiation should be performed in sacrifice, altar, house, journey, temple, river works and study; in the founding of a city and laying of foundation, a pure-minded person should perform auspicious rites; work done in a city by those without rites is fearful, short-lived and always inauspicious.

items.note: Roles at a city's founding: astrologer and priest perform śānti, the priest offers oblation, the astrologer fixes stability, the sthapati makes offerings.
items.gloss: Work done without shastra knowledge, without characteristics and without the rites is inauspicious and fruitless; after the astrologer and priest perform the propitiatory rites, the shastra-knowing sthapati should do the work; the priest offers oblation in fire, the astrologer gives stability, the sthapati makes offerings; when deities installed at the city's centre and crossroads are constantly worshipped, peace prevails in that city.

items.note: Spacing between city (pura), kheṭa and village; street intervals of 30, 20 and 10 dhanus.
items.gloss: Kheta, its half vikrama, its half grama; a kheta lies one yojana (about sixteen miles) from the city, a village one yojana from the kheta, and village to village a gavyuti (two kos, about six km); the boundary of a vishaya is two kos, half of it for a city; in a city roads on the directions are thirty dhanus apart, in a kheta twenty, in a village ten.

items.note: Quarters of the city by occupation begin: fire-workers and goldsmiths south-east; merchants, gamblers, actors south.
items.gloss: Settle all those who live by fire, including goldsmiths, and other labourers in the south-east; build in the south the houses of vaishya merchants, gamblers and rogues, oil-pressers and actors and dancers.

items.note: Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra's allotment of city quarters by occupation: swineherds and hunters south-west, charioteers west, officials north-west, ascetics' shelters, Brahmin assembly and rest-houses north, ghee and fruit sellers north-east.
items.gloss: Swineherds, shepherds, hunters, fishermen and officers of punishment in the south-west; those skilled in chariots and weapons in the west; officials of various works, servants and liquor-sellers in the north-west; shelters of ascetics, the Brahmin assembly, water-sheds and charitable halls (punyashala) in the north; ghee and fruit sellers in the north-east.

items.note: Varṇas assigned to directions; Śaiva/sectarian ascetics (liṅgasthas) settled east outside the town, cremation ground south.
items.gloss: Brahmins in the east, kshatriyas in the west, vaishyas and shudras in the south and north respectively; merchants, physicians and chiefs in all four directions; the army especially on the four sides; outside the town in the east settle the lingasthas (Shaiva or sectarians); the wise sthapati should place the cremation ground and its inhabitants in the south.

items.note: Siting and orientation of temples (devasadana) within and outside the town relative to the rampart and moat.
items.gloss: On the four sides, starting from rampart and moat, outside at one hundred fifty or two hundred dhanus or up to a hundred, build the abodes of the gods with their attendants' houses, each with its prasada, facing the city, auspicious, in pleasant groves; inside and outside the middle of a north-south long city build temples; in the east make them face west, in the west face east, on the south and north sides facing south and north respectively.

items.note: Directional placement of deities' temples outside the town: Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Indra, Dharma east; Gaṇeśa, Mātṛkās, Yama south; Bhadrakālī south-west; river and Varuṇa west.
items.gloss: Build the temples of Vishnu, Surya, Indra and Dharma in the east; Sanatkumara, Savitri, Maruts and Marut in the south-east; Ganesha, the Matrikas, Bhutas and Yamaraja in the south; Bhadrakali's temple and ancestors' chaitya in the south-west; temples of the ocean, rivers, Vishvakarma, Prajapati and Varuna in the west.

items.note: Continuation of directional placement: nāgas, Śani, Kātyāyanī north-west; Viśākha, Skanda, Soma, Kubera north; Maheśa, Śrī, Agni north-east; deities well placed bring the city prosperity.
items.gloss: Temples of the Nagas, Shanaishchara and Katyayani in the north-west; Vishakha, Skanda, Soma and Kubera separately in the north; the charming temple of Jagadguru Mahesha, Shri and Agni in the north-east; the place of Uma's lord is everywhere around the city on rivers, seas, forests and mountains; deities installed in their own directions bring the city due growth and joy.

items.note: Same placement rules inside the city: Brahmā, Indra, Kṛṣṇa-Balarāma temples in the middle; shrines of mother goddesses, yakṣas, Gaṇeśa, Śiva and bhūtas on road-ways.
items.gloss: The arrangement of temples outside the city should be the same inside, each in its own direction; in the centre of the city build the temples of Brahma, Indra and Krishna-Balarama; on the roads of mothers, yakshas, Ganesha, Shivaka and groups of bhutas place shrines.

items.note: Rule: no house, village, temple or town should be built larger in measure or quality than the earlier.
items.gloss: Each house, each village, each temple and each town should not be made greater in size and quality than the earlier one.
